notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded non-regional IEEE 1516.1-2025 timestamped Delete Object Instance, timestamped Remove Object Instance, Retract, and Request Retraction surfaces to the official C++ declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. The linked Catch2 scenarios demonstrate lower-bound validation, pre-delivery retraction and reconstitution, exact-bound callback ordering, timestamp/order/retraction propagation, the supplied tag and producing federate, sender exclusion, and a time-6 removal that makes a later time-7 directed interaction stale. Focused Connection Lost scenarios additionally retain marked time-5 and time-6 Remove Object Instance callbacks through the faulted regulator's configured unconditional-divest cleanup, preserving the official callback fields before the survivor's matching time-6 grant; the DELETE_OBJECTS companion confirms it remains timestamped rather than becoming automatic receive-order removal, and a staggered two-survivor case keeps the object state until both callback boundaries complete. A separate mixed nonconstrained/time-constrained scenario proves legal post-delivery retraction: it reconstitutes the object/name/known state and committed split ownership before Request Retraction reaches the delivered recipient, while suppressing the constrained recipient's pending removal. A focused terminalization scenario proves that an expired deletion designator remains MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted while its heavyweight snapshot, deletion marker, and released name no longer block a new registration. A second scenario confirms an owner who resigns after delivered removal is neither reconstituted nor notified, and its former attribute remains unowned. Complete alternate-advance, Disable Time Regulation/re-enable, save/restore recovery, active in-flight ownership, other producer/recipient resignation, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
